paragraphs.text: Media preview for DSH: video and audio in the right-Sidebar document preview, with HTTP Range stream
ing and desktop seek.
# dsh-preview-media
Video and audio preview for DeepSeek Harness: play `mp4`, `mov`, `mkv`, `webm` and `mp3`, `flac`, `w
av` right inside the right-Sidebar document preview instead of the built-in “this format cannot be p
reviewed” empty state.
**中文** | English (this file) · 中文说明
## Why
The built-in preview registers renderers for text, code, Markdown, images, PDF, HTML, Office and spr
eadsheets, and lists video/audio suffixes as *known binary containers with no renderer* — so opening
a video shows an icon and one line of text. This plugin registers those suffixes and draws the brow
ser's native player, fed by an authenticated streaming route that honours HTTP `Range`, so seeking w
orks and a 2 GB file is never loaded into memory or into the conversation.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then restart the desktop app (a profile patch change is read at boot). No configuration is required;
the defaults cover the common suffixes.
To check it loaded, open any `.mp4` from the Files tab: the preview pane shows the player rather tha
n the unsupported-format notice.
## What it does
- **Renderer** — registers two document-previews implementations, `dsh-preview-media/video` (video s
uffixes) and `dsh-preview-media/audio` (audio suffixes), with priority `extension`, `loading: 'rende

rer'`, and their suffixes declared binary so the “plain text” fallback is not offered.
- **Player**
— a native `<video>`/`<audio>` element with the browser's own controls. The video is fitted into the
pane with `object-fit: contain` inside a flexible frame, so a portrait or landscape clip is fully v
isible at once, with black letterboxing instead of spilling past the preview edge. Below it sit **倍速
**全屏 / Full screen** and **画中画 / Picture in picture**. Speed and loop also apply to audio, and the c
hoice is remembered per browser. Audio shows a card with the file name, its size and the player. The
body reports `loaded` / `failed` back to the document preview owner so the tab's loading state sett

les.
- **Stream** — a Host route `GET|HEAD /api/preview/media?path=<absolute path>` that answers `20
0` with `Accept-Ranges: bytes`, `206` with `Content-Range` for one byte window, `416` with `Content-
Range: bytes */size` for an unsatisfiable window, and `HEAD` with headers only. It reads the file a
chunk at a time (`chunkBytes`, 1 MiB by default) through `ctx.fs.readByteRange`, so memory stays fla

t.
- **Desktop seeking** — the desktop app serves the page from `dsh-app://app` and proxies every re
quest through `protocol.handle`. Chromium's media stack cannot seek a response produced by a custom-
protocol handler (`video.seekable` collapses to `[0, 0]`), so in the desktop shell the player would
play but a dragged timeline would snap back to the start. The Host therefore also listens on an ephe
meral `127.0.0.1` port and hands the browser half a capability token (`GET /api/preview/media?discov
er=1`); in the shell the player streams from that loopback origin, where normal HTTP `Range` makes s

eeking work. In a plain browser the authenticated route is used as before.
[该节后续省略]
## Configuration
Settings live on the `preview-media` entry (Settings → Plugins, or the profile patch). Every key has
a code-side default, so a partial config is valid.
| Key | Default | Meaning |
| `enabled` | `true` | Mount the route at all. _Off_ leaves the renderer registered but transfers no

bytes (`503`). |
| `routePath` | `/api/preview/media` | Route pathname. Must start with `/api/`; an

ything else falls back to the default so the auth fence still applies. |
| `loopback` | `true` | Als
o serve bytes from the token-guarded `127.0.0.1` origin. This is what makes the desktop player seeka

ble. _Off_ keeps only the authenticated route: the desktop shell can play but not seek. |
| `debug`
| `false` | Append playback/loopback diagnostics to `$DSH_HOME/preview-media-debug.log`. Leave off u

nless you are diagnosing a problem. |
| `maxBytes` | `2147483648` (2 GiB) | Largest file served; lar

ger files answer `413`. |
| `chunkBytes` | `1048576` | Bytes per ranged read. |
| `videoExtensions`
| `mp4, m4v, mov, webm, ogv, ogg, mkv, avi, wmv, flv, 3gp, ts, m2ts, mts` | Suffixes the video playe

r claims. |
| `audioExtensions` | `mp3, wav, flac, m4a, aac, oga, opus, weba, wma, aiff, aif` | Suff
ixes the audio player claims. |
The browser half mirrors the suffix lists in `lib/client.js`; keep them in sync when changing either
side. The route path is published to the page as `__DSH_PREVIEW_MEDIA_CONFIG__` by the Host, so a c
onfigured path and the player's URL never drift apart.
## Playback support
Playback depends on the browser's own codecs, not on this plugin. Chromium/Electron plays MP4 (H.264
/AAC), WebM (VP8/VP9/Opus), Ogg and most audio formats. **Matroska (`.mkv`) and AVI usually do not d
ecode** in Chromium; the player then reports “浏览器不支持这个编码 / This codec is not supported by the browse
r” and the _Open in app_ control in the preview header still hands the file to the system player. Re
muxing such files to MP4/WebM is the reliable fix.
## How it is built
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The browser half is a hand-written module-loader bundle (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory
})`) with `react` and `react/jsx-runtime` as its only module-table requests, so it needs no build s
tep and cannot drift from the Host's React copy.
## Known limitations
- One byte window per request; a multi-range `Range` header is answered `416`. Browsers only ever as

k a media element for one window.
- `.mkv`, `.avi`, `.wmv`, `.flv` are claimed and listed, but Chrom
ium cannot decode them; the plugin shows the player's error state rather than pretending they play.

- No playlist, subtitle-track or speed controls of its own — the native controls own those.
- If a d
eployment blocks the loopback origin (firewall, policy), the player falls back to the authenticated
route automatically: the file still plays, but the desktop timeline is not seekable again. That is a
n Electron limitation (electron#38749, electron#51442), not something the route can fix.
